pages.title: How to print output
pages.content:
Cool - so you learnt how to accept integer inputs.

Now let's look at how to convert input into output and display the same.

Most algorithmic programming problems will need you to generate the following types of output
- Integers or Floats
- Strings
- An array of integers or strings

Go ahead and try in the IDE.\
Click on **Submit** to proceed.

questions.question: Which method writes text followed by a newline in C#?
questions.explanation: Console.WriteLine writes to standard output and appends a newline.

questions.question: Which type is appropriate for a whole-number variable?
questions.explanation: int is used for ordinary whole-number values.

questions.question: How do you convert a numeric string to int?
questions.explanation: int.Parse converts a valid numeric string to an integer.

questions.question: What does Split() commonly help with?
options: Separating tokens in an input line
questions.explanation: Split separates a line into tokens.

questions.question: What should a solution do with each test case when T is given?
questions.explanation: T specifies how many independent cases follow.

questions.question: Which statement is true about hidden tests?
options: They can expose edge cases not shown in samples
They are always identical to samples
They are comments in the source
questions.explanation: Hidden tests are intended to check broader correctness.

questions.question: Why are custom inputs useful?
options: They let you probe your own edge cases
questions.explanation: Custom inputs are useful for targeted debugging.

questions.question: What is the usual purpose of Run before Submit?
questions.explanation: Run is useful for local checks before final judging.

questions.question: Which expression reads one full input line?
questions.explanation: Console.ReadLine reads a line from standard input.

questions.question: Why should input format be followed exactly?
options: The judge parses input according to that format
questions.explanation: A judge supplies data according to the documented input contract.

pages.title: How to solve programming problems
pages.content:
In the previous modules - we solved simple programming problems that had a direct approach.\
In this module, we will cover problems that focus on logic building. Some suggestions for this module:
- Use a pen and paper to work out solutions.\
The logic / algorithm first has to be clear in your mind before you decide to code it out.
- Don't spend more than 30 minutes on any problem. While the objective is to learn - if you don't know the approach, it's best to learn the concept / review the solution.

For Beginner's level programming problems - we think the following works best
- **Step 1**: Understand the problem statement and the sample test cases
- **Step 2**: Generate examples - Create 10 input and output cases of your own
- **Step 3**: Observations / Pattern - Observe your examples to identify the logic
- **Step 4**: Plan your code - Modularise and solve sub-components of your problem
- **Step 5**: Learn - You may come across components of your logic where you don't know how to execute the code. \
In such cases, ask Google or ChatGPT or your friends and learn!
- **Step 6**: Write the code - For simpler programming problems - C++ solutions will be less than 20 lines in more than 95% of the cases.
- **Step 7**: Identify edge cases - If your code still fails - try and and come up with corner cases where your code may fail
